Python source, tests, or Python-facing behavior changes

write_policy.notes: The manager carries agreed scope, handoff and results in the current conversation and Git. Selected reader-facing reports use their existing owners.
The manager reviewer approves or challenges scope, acceptance criteria, source-bucket separation, and specialist activation.

The designer produces the detailed design document before coding begins, including reuse-first choices, a Design Side-Effect Map, identifier naming plan, and the existing writing/style conventions to follow.

The design reviewer independently checks the detailed design document, implementation readiness, Design Side-Effect Map, identifier naming plan, and whether existing code, naming, and writing style are being followed. This is the most important pre-implementation review gate.

The document-flow reviewer reads the document linearly from the top and checks whether a first reader can follow the meaning and reader-visible side effects without backtracking. It stays separate from the design reviewer.

The test designer returns an activation decision first and is activated only after the owning production design or algorithm contract and implementation mechanism are established or repaired, when a concrete unresolved oracle, specification, regression, or failure-mode risk remains outside static analysis, existing checkers, and targeted validation.

The implementer may modify repository files only inside the agreed task scope carried by the parent handoff and current Git diff. Multiple write-capable roles require disjoint scopes in the current checkout; colliding writers must be serialized into later waves. Independent streams use the repository-topic lifecycle's prepared linked-worktree for a parent/same-repository branch or independent-clone for a dependency repository. WORKTREE_SCOPE.md is legacy cleanup/drift evidence, not scope authority. It must extend existing code, mirror existing style, follow approved naming before introducing any new pattern.

The implementation reviewer is the single owning review dispatch. It performs one initial review per candidate epoch, emits stable blocking finding IDs separately from advisory notes, and after repair runs only a focused recheck of addressed blockers and invalidated evidence. Python/C++ reviewers validate distinct selected claims and do not create duplicate full-review workflows.

The final reviewer is the terminal ship gate for the current candidate epoch. It reads the stable open blocker set and selected validation result, does not restart broad review, and approves or hands back when blockers and unresolved request clauses are zero. Advisory improvements are separate work.
Verification may update only the verification artifact.

Audit closeout records the requested outcome, actual validation and delivery results, workflow monitoring, agent evaluation, and retrospective evidence. The auditor confirms unresolved request clauses and blocking findings are accounted for, selected validation results are accurate, focused rechecks are complete when selected, required diff-check evidence is present when selected, and workflow-monitoring plus evaluation feedback are resolved.

write_policy.notes: The integration executor owns normal merge/conflict resolution, origin/main readback, and integration receipt; the parent only relays dependency order and status.
The publisher owns authorized Issue/PR writes and remote readback; the parent does not draft or publish GitHub mutations.
Research findings are recorded in research notes, not direct repo edits.
The research reviewer checks source quality and whether the proposed research actually supports the plan.

The experimenter may write only run artifacts and runtime output directories explicitly assigned in the current run handoff. WORKTREE_SCOPE.md is legacy cleanup/drift evidence and is not runtime output scope authority. It may not edit repository source files.
The experiment reviewer critiques fairness, comparison targets, interpretation, and whether the next code change is actually justified by the evidence.
Execution planning stays in the report bundle and must assign explicit stage owners, review separation, and subagent activation before detailed design begins.
The schedule reviewer checks execution order, reviewer separation, milestone realism, explicit stage activation, and sequencing risk. It must remain distinct from the design reviewer.
The citation-evidence reviewer checks whether reader-facing claims point to actual citations, figures, tables, derivations, or results and whether the cited support matches what the text says.
The notation-definition reviewer checks whether symbols, abbreviations, technical terms, units, indices, and assumptions are defined before use and used consistently.
The logic-gap reviewer checks whether major claims are supported, whether inferential jumps are explicit, and whether results are kept separate from interpretation.
Infra stewardship proposes and reviews infra changes, while the implementer applies repo edits.
The infra reviewer checks rollout, safety, and maintenance cost before coding begins.
The reproducibility reviewer records rerunability findings only in the perspective review artifact.
The scientific computing reviewer records workflow and engineering findings only in the perspective review artifact.
The benchmark reviewer records fairness and confounder findings only in the perspective review artifact.
The artifact reviewer records bundle-readiness findings only in the perspective review artifact.
The fair data reviewer records metadata and reuse findings only in the perspective review artifact.
The ML-science reviewer records reporting and overclaim findings only in the perspective review artifact.
The project reviewer records repo-wide inventory and integration findings only in the project review artifact.

Terra is a conditional read-only cross-cutting specialist candidate. It returns an owner closure, context capsule, and accepted/rejected/escalated handback to the Sol parent; it does not coordinate, implement, become a general worker, or activate without evidence.
The docs-workflow steward records canon and adapter findings only in the docs-workflow review artifact.
The prompt-config reviewer records prompt, routing, and subagent-config findings only in the prompt-config review artifact.

The Python reviewer is a bounded domain validator selected by change_reviewer for a distinct Python claim. It records type, test, and lint findings only in the python review artifact and does not make the owning review decision.

The C++ reviewer is a bounded domain validator selected by change_reviewer for a distinct native claim. It records native build, ABI, ownership, and test findings only in the C++ review artifact and does not make the owning review decision.
The report reviewer records report-structure and evidence-traceability findings only in the report review artifact.

The skill evaluator returns only the fixed observed report grammar as an artifact; the parent stores it in agent_evaluation.md, scores it, owns iteration and convergence decisions, and finalizes feedback_actions_resolved and learning_capture_complete outside evaluator context.

The mathematical correctness reviewer is a Luna-backed read-only logical role. It records its math-scope findings in the existing change review artifact, checks the mathematical intent packet and mapped changed paths, and cannot authorize architecture, framework, JIT, compiler, backend, runtime, container, routing, environment, common-infrastructure, or proof-tool edits.

team.summary: Select roles for the agreed task. Codex provides agent execution and collaboration; Git and the current conversation carry scope, handoff and results. Preserve role models, selected reviews, experiment/proof artifacts, hook logs and Eval.
